## 1. What is actually broken, in fix order

The 48 findings collapse to 14 defects. Duplicates are merged; the finding numbers in brackets are the survey's.

### Tier 1: destroys work or lies about what was made

**1. Single-letter shortcuts fire behind open dialogs, and Space activates nothing.** [4, 5, 24, 36]
One handler, `studio.html:3124-3135`. It guards `INPUT/TEXTAREA/SELECT/contentEditable` and nothing else. Three separate consequences: Space on any focused button rerolls the seed instead of pressing the button (13 header buttons, panel switches, `role=\"tab\"` elements, all confirmed); `s`, `f`, `e`, `r` drive the app behind an open About or Settings; and Space on the Settings Apply button rerolls the seed while the textarea still holds the old one, after which Apply silently reverts the plate through `Object.assign(own(e2.state), obj)` at `studio.html:3010`.

Fix, in the same six lines:
- After the Escape branch, return early when `MODALS.map($).some(m => m && !m.hidden)`. `MODALS` is at `studio.html:1965`; the Tab focus trap at `studio.html:3100-3113` already keeps Tab inside the dialog, so only Escape needs to pass.
- Reorder the Escape branch: close an open modal first, fall through to `setFocus(false)` only when nothing is open. Today `focusMode` is tested first, so Escape inside a dialog in focus mode restores the chrome and leaves the dialog up.
- Before the Space branch, also bail when the target is `BUTTON`, `[role=\"switch\"]`, `[role=\"tab\"]`, `A[href]` or `SUMMARY`, so Space reaches the browser's own activation. Space-to-generate on `document.body` is documented at `studio.html:719` and must survive.

**2. The URL hash never follows the plate.** [8, 13, 38, 39]
`writeHash()` is at `studio.html:1553` and is called from exactly one place, the Copy Link handler at `:3035`. `scheduleHash()` at `studio.html:1562` is dead code. So Generate, a typed seed, a slider, Surprise and a tab switch all leave the address bar describing a different plate, on occasion a different technique: the verifier switched to Ising and the hash still read `#tilings/penrose-1974` while the title read Ising. Reload, Back, bookmark and browser restore all discard the work. In a studio whose entire premise is reprint-from-a-seed, this is the deepest defect in the file.

Fix: call `scheduleHash()` from the same points that call `snapshot()`: the end of `regenerate`, the commit path of `setParam`, after `switchTo`, after `surprise`, after a settings apply, on slider pointerup. It is already debounced at 180 ms and already uses `replaceState` behind `hashSilent`, so the back stack stays clean and `applyHash` does not re-enter. While in `parseHash` (`studio.html:1536-1551`), fix two neighbours: wrap the `decodeURIComponent(parts[1])` seed decode in its own try/catch (`#tilings/%zz` currently throws an uncaught URIError and toasts it), and distinguish \"no hash\" from \"unknown id\" so a stale link says `No technique called \"x\" in this build` instead of silently booting a random tab with a random seed. Separately decide whether the `pageshow` handler at `studio.html:3197` should reroll the seed on a bfcache restore. It should not; that is the same loss by another route.

**3. Penrose exports a different picture than the plate.** [3, 6]
`exportSVG` at `studio.html:7874` disagrees with `render()` at `studio.html:7587` on three things: it strokes every polygon in `s.bg` (the paper colour) at a literal `stroke-width=\"0.4\"` in a 6000-unit viewBox, where the canvas uses `pal[Math.min(np-1, s.strokeColor)]` at `lwBase = max(0.35*h/900, s.strokeWidth*sc*0.035)`; it colours `gen` fills by the raw loop index `i` instead of `mix32(tiles.anc[i]+7) & 1023` with `jitterRamp`; and it skips `insetPoly`. Measured: 21.30 per cent dark pixels and 89 colours on screen against 0.00 per cent and 34 colours in the print. The rhomb mosaic collapses to flat orange stars. Line 7875 is the only place in the file that strokes with `s.bg`; every other exportSVG uses `U.inkFor(s.bg)`. This reaches the PNG too, because `doExport` at `studio.html:2748` rasterizes `exportSVG` whenever a module provides one and never calls the module's own `exportPNG`.

Fix: make `exportSVG` take the same three decisions `render()` takes. Then add the regression, because this class of bug is invisible in a thumbnail and the file has shipped it before: `tools/export.js` gains a plate-versus-print comparison at a common 300x300 downsample, run over every module with an `exportSVG`, failing above a few levels per channel. The floor is already measured: aztec 4.8, sle 0.26, Penrose 20.8.

**4. Chladni prints a different picture in two of its four styles.** [21]
`exportSVG` at `studio.html:11858` hardcodes `lw = max(0.4, min(W,H)/900)` and reads neither `s.threshold` nor `s.softness`, so the plate's swelling bands print as a uniform hairline. Worse, it ignores `s.style` entirely: in Filled field the plate is a dense grey and red field and the print is a bare contour drawing (MAD 102.2); Sand does the same. The \"dotted fragments\" symptom the finder reported is not real; it is a downsampling artifact of a 2.67 px line into a 300 px thumbnail.

Fix: have `exportSVG` return nothing for `filled` and `sand` so `doExport` falls through to the module's own `exportPNG`, which renders them correctly. For `nodal` and `contour`, derive the stroke from `s.threshold` and `s.softness` the way `computeToImageData` does, or emit the band as a filled region between two threshold contours, and scale `n` with the requested output.

**5. Visiting about 17 GPU tabs kills the earlier ones permanently and silently.** [7]
30 tab visits produced 20 contexts, 4 lost, 0 restored, and the lost tabs stayed dead for the session: `gl.isContextLost()` true, a 48x48 readback all zeros, `#fault` hidden, no toast, and the status line still reporting `step 588`. Generate and Reset do not recover it. `showFault` is behind `if (currentId === mod.id)` at `studio.html:1895`, so a background eviction is never surfaced; `switchTo` at `studio.html:2220` never looks at `e.contextLost`; and `rebuildEntry` at `studio.html:2888` is reachable only from the fault panel's Try again button at `:3068`.

Fix, two independent halves. Keep a bounded LRU of live instances and dispose the oldest in `switchTo`, removing its canvas, so contexts are released deliberately rather than taken. And have `switchTo` call `rebuildEntry` when it lands on an entry with `e.contextLost` set, since `webglcontextrestored` demonstrably never fires for an evicted context.

**6. The seed field is a 2 px sliver at every width anyone uses, and is unreachable by mouse or keyboard.** [1, 2]
`.seedbox` at `studio.html:160` is `display:flex` with `overflow:hidden` and no `flex` declaration, so it inherits `0 1 auto` with `min-width:auto` and is crushed by `.brand { margin-right: auto }` plus 20 siblings in a nowrap row. Measured width is exactly 2 px from 320 through 2200 CSS px. `#seed` still lays out at 96-130 px, outside its clipped parent. `elementFromPoint` at the dice centre returns `HEADER.bar`; a real click there changes nothing. Focusing `#seed` by script scrolls the box to `scrollLeft 134` and puts the input at `left=58`, behind the wordmark. Not a font artifact: forcing Arial, Helvetica and Arial Narrow all leave it at 2 px.

Fix: `flex: 0 0 auto` plus an explicit min-width, matching what `.printbox` already has at `studio.html:161`. Do not land this alone: `.seedbox`'s scrollWidth is 180 px against a used width of 2, so exempting it adds 178 px to a bar that already overflows. Ship it with item 7. Also: `#headline` carries the `hidden` attribute but `.seedbox { display: flex }` beats the UA `[hidden] { display: none }`, so above 1480 px (the `#headline { display: none !important }` rule lives at `studio.html:251`, not 1560) a second empty bordered box paints. Move that to a `[hidden] { display: none !important }` rule so the markup means what it says.

### Tier 2: the print lies about itself

**7. The toolbar overflows at every real width and the print controls are the part that falls off.** [9, 12, 20, 22, 25]
`.bar` is `flex-wrap: nowrap; overflow-x: auto` with no mask fade, while its sibling `.tabs` carries the full `.scrollable` / `.at-start` / `.at-end` treatment at `studio.html:230-233`. Overflow is roughly 200-350 px at 1280-1920 and over 1000 px at 390. `.printbox` and `#btn-export` are the clipped children at every desktop width. Reachability is real but poor: shift+wheel scrolls it, Tab reaches Export, `E` opens the modal. What is genuinely wrong is that on a tool whose output is a print, the print size, the ppi and the Colophon toggle are invisible and unhinted at every width a person actually uses. Full fix in section 2.

**8. The colophon states the sheet size where the artwork's size belongs.** [26, 44]
`composeSheet` at `studio.html:2722` prints `inTxt(sp.wIn)` and `inTxt(sp.hIn)`, which are the sheet, while the image is drawn at the `artW/artH` computed at `studio.html:2671-2673` from `innerW` minus the caption band. Measured: growth at 8 in captions itself `6.4 x 8.0 in` when the art is 5.11 x 6.39 in, a 24 per cent overstatement on the long edge. The same wrong pair appears in `updateColoPreview` (`:2594`) and the modal's print note (`:2755`), so all three agree with each other and disagree with the file. Fix: have `sheetLayout` return `artW/artH` and feed those into all three, phrased `image 6.1 x 6.1 in on an 8.0 x 8.0 in sheet`.

In the same function, the caption type is sized from sheet pixels: `fs.meta = max(7, sheetW * 0.0085)` and `fs.p = max(6, sheetW * 0.0072)` at `studio.html:2654-2658`, which is a fixed 0.6 and 0.5 pt per inch of sheet width regardless of ppi. At 8 in / 300 ppi that is 4.15 pt and 3.32 pt. The 6 and 7 px floors are 1.4 and 1.7 pt and never engage. Fix: derive from physical inches, `fs = max(minPt, ...) / 72 * dpi`, floors of 7 pt for the parameter block and 8 pt for the meta line, with band height and margin from the same numbers.

**9. The print menu offers combinations that cannot render.** [27]
`printSpec` at `studio.html:2528-2536` clamps against `MAX_EDGE 16000` and `MAX_AREA 132e6` and never reads `MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE`, though every GL module throws on it at export time (`:4975, :6288, :9124, :9518, :11319, :13574`). At 28 in / 300 ppi the readout confidently says `8,400 x 8,400 px` and the export fails. Fix: read `MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE` once at boot from a throwaway context, fold it into the clamp, disable or mark the impossible options for the current aspect, and name the largest reachable size in the failure text.

**10. Attractors prints half the exposure of the preview.** [28]
`studio.html:6930` sets `target = Math.min(EXPORT_CAP, Math.max(s.points, A.count))`, so the same 4M points land on 11.1x the pixels: 2.8 hits per pixel on screen, 0.25 in the print. Measured mean luminance 20.0 against 10.2, and the bright veins break into speckle. Fix: `target = min(EXPORT_CAP, s.points * (W*H)/(A.W*A.H))`, and when the cap bites, say so in the export note the way `fieldNote` already does for grid-limited tabs.

**11. Every tab opens on a screen of prose.** [14]
Across all 63 tabs (the survey's count) at 1440x900, 48 show zero controls on the opening screen; median first control at 999 px; the Color group starts below one panel height on 63 of 63, median 2,329 px. The fix is half-built: the \"What this is\" block at `studio.html:2400-2412` is a `<details>` whose open state is already persisted under `STORE + 'about'`. Flip the default at `:2402` to `localStorage.getItem(STORE + 'about') === '1'`. Measured payoff on Liesegang: first control 1,561 to 611 px, visible controls 0 to 3. Then move the Color group directly under the first parameter group instead of last.

**12. A long export freezes the page for minutes with a frozen note and no cancel.** [29]
Pendulum at the smallest offered size ran 253-411 s with 8-second windows where no JS ran at all, so the modal's close button cannot answer a click. `#export-note` is written once at `studio.html:2746` and never rewritten. Fix in order of value: shorten the yield interval so the page never goes 8 s without running JS; rewrite the note from host-side progress (tile k of n, points of target); then a Cancel button backed by an abort flag, checked at each yield. Do not thread the abort flag through every module; add it to the tiled GL export path only.

### Tier 3: correctness of the small stuff

Batch these; each is a few lines.

- **Light theme fails WCAG AA** [18]. `#btn-generate` 3.86, `#status` 3.83, `.witness-hint` 3.83, `.live-fp` 4.02, `.printbox label` 4.41. Dark passes everywhere. Darken `--muted` in the light `:root` from `#726C63` to about `#635D54`, and set `.btn.primary` colour to `--panel` rather than `--accent-ink`. Re-run the probe.
- **Focus mode leaves the page with one tab stop** [19]. `setFocus(on)` toggles a class and refits and does nothing about focus; 93 tab stops become 1. Give `#stage` `tabindex=\"-1\"` and focus it, render a persistent Exit control inside the stage, and return focus to `#btn-focus` on exit.
- **`V` starts a recording on a Still plate** [41], guaranteeing a \"Nothing was recorded\" toast. Route the key through the same `liveNow` test `updateRecordUI` already uses at `studio.html:2090`.
- **`file://` greets the user with an error toast** [23]. `navigator.serviceWorker.getRegistrations()` at `studio.html:3205` has no `.catch`, and the `unhandledrejection` handler toasts it. This hits real users because the launchers in `/home/user/GENChase/run/` fall back to opening the file directly. Skip the block when `location.protocol === 'file:'` and attach `.catch(() => {})` anyway.
- **Gallery is the one dialog that does not close on an outside click** [40]. Add the overlay handler beside the existing wiring at `studio.html:3032`.
- **reduced-motion misses the two infinite pulses** [34]. `studio.html:595` covers `transition` only; add `animation: none !important`.
- **The tab strip focus ring is clipped top and bottom** [35] by `nav.tabs` overflow with zero vertical padding. Use an inset `box-shadow` ring with `outline-offset: 0`, or give the nav a few pixels of vertical padding.
- **Tooltips and the shortcut list** [45]. `#btn-generate`, `#btn-export` and `#btn-about` carry no `title`; the whole shortcut list is the last sentence of an 11,083-character paragraph, starting at index 3,057. Add the three titles and lift the shortcuts into their own `<h3>` and key/action table near the top of the modal.
- **Keyboard poke** [17]. 24 modules implement `disturb(p)` and the canvas has `tabIndex: -1`; there is no keyboard path at all. Give the pokeable canvas `tabindex=\"0\"`, arrows to move a crosshair in normalised plate coordinates, Enter to apply, Shift+arrow to drag. Update the hint at `studio.html:2147` when the canvas has focus. The finder's \"needs a real accessible name\" half is wrong; the `aria-label` is already there.
- **Witness tick** [42]. Already gated on `!document.hidden`. Back the 400 ms interval off to a few seconds once the plate has been Still for a few ticks, and skip it entirely while `e.paused`. Nothing more, for reasons in section 4.

## 2. The mobile layout decision

**Yes. Build a fixed bottom dock below 760 px, and put the print group in it.** The owner's instinct is right and the measurements support it twice over.

The phone top bar fails in two directions at once. Horizontally, `.bar` is 1,531 px wide in a 390 px viewport holding 20 children, with `#btn-export` at x=1402 and `.printbox` at x=1157; the visible row is the wordmark, Presets, Surprise and half of Generate. Vertically, at 390x844 the document is 2,269 px tall and the stage is `position: sticky` at 46vh, so at scrollY 700 there is not one button on screen: `.bar` bottom is at -644, `.tabs` bottom at -607, `#btn-generate` and `#btn-export` both at -689. The plate stays pinned and every verb that acts on it is gone. Moving the buttons to a fixed dock fixes both problems with one rule. Nothing else does.

**What goes in the dock**, left to right: `Generate` (primary, takes the slack), the inches select, the ppi select, the Colophon toggle, `Export`. Five controls, one row, and above them the print dimension readout on its own line. Generate and Export are the only two verbs; the print group is the only thing that changes what Export produces, and separating them means a person has to find a different scrolling row to alter what the button in front of them will do. The readout goes here because today it is invisible at every width under 1801 px (`studio.html:247`) and the 980 px rule written to rescue it (`studio.html:570-577`) sets `flex-basis`, border and `white-space` but never restores `display`, so it has never painted on any screen. The dock is the first place it has ever had a home. The clamped-ppi suffix rides in that same element, and it is the part that changes what comes off the printer.

**What stays at the top**: the brand, the seed box, Presets, and the tab strip. The seed is the identity of the plate and has to be readable and typable; it belongs next to the wordmark, not in an action dock. The tab strip stays at the top because it is navigation, not action, and because a second fixed row at the bottom would eat the plate.

**Everything else goes behind one More button** in the top row, opening a sheet that lists Surprise, Link, Save, Gallery, Undo, Reset, Timeline, Focus, Ambient, About, JSON and Panel side with their shortcut letters. That is twelve controls removed from the row, which is what actually cures the overflow. Asking a person to swipe 1,100 px past 16 buttons is not an affordance problem to be solved with a gradient.

**Safe area and browser chrome.** The dock is `position: fixed; left: 0; right: 0; bottom: 0` with `padding-bottom: max(10px, env(safe-area-inset-bottom))`, and `body` gets a matching bottom padding so the last panel control is not trapped under it. Use `fixed`, not `sticky`: iOS Safari's collapsing URL bar moves the layout viewport, and a sticky element anchored to a `100vh` ancestor drifts under the toolbar. For the same reason, change the sticky stage from `46vh` to `46dvh` at `studio.html:589`; the `.app` rule at `:155` already pairs `100vh` with `100dvh` and the stage should match.

**Fix the landscape bug in the same pass.** `.app { min-height: 560px }` at `studio.html:155` makes an 844x390 landscape phone scroll: the art canvas ends at y=520 in a 390 px viewport and the status line at y=532 is entirely off-screen. Drop it to 0 or gate it behind a `min-height` media query, and add a short-viewport rule around `@media (max-height: 560px)` that trims the bar and tab strip so `.main` takes the remainder. Chrome eats 93 px of a 390 px landscape viewport today, 24 per cent. Verify with a real resize event, not a style injection, because the canvas is sized by JS.

**Raise the single-column breakpoint from 760 to 900.** A 768 portrait tablet falls just outside the narrow layout today and gets the worst of both: the art canvas is 422x422, 22.6 per cent of the screen, `.side` takes 290 px, 509 px of stage height is empty, and both escapes (`#btn-focus` at x=927, `#btn-side` at x=1198) are off the right edge of a 768 px viewport. The dock plus the single-column layout fixes that tablet for free.

**Desktop changes too, but not to a dock.** Above 900 px there is no dock. Instead:

- `.printbox` and `#btn-export` become `position: sticky; right: 0` inside `.bar`, with a `--panel` background and a left border, so the two print-critical controls are never off-screen at any width.
- `.bar` gets the `.scrollable` / `.at-start` / `.at-end` mask fade that `.tabs` already carries at `studio.html:230-233`, toggled by the same code at `:2932`. Two scrolling rows in the same header should not behave differently.
- The same More sheet absorbs the secondary buttons below about 1400 px.
- Move the `.printbox .dims` hide from 1800 px down to about 1100 px, and add `display: flex` to the 980 px block so it finally takes effect.

**Reject wrapping `.bar` onto two rows on desktop.** Two 56 px rows plus a 37 px tab strip is 149 px of chrome in a 900 px window, and the landscape finding already shows what chrome costs. Sticky-right plus an overflow sheet gets the same result for 37 px.

## 3. The navigation problem

At 1440x900 the strip is 5,982 px wide showing 14 of 63 tabs (the survey's count; there are 117 now), with `scrollbar-width: none` and `.tabs::-webkit-scrollbar { display: none }`, so there is nothing to drag, and a plain vertical wheel over it moves neither the strip nor the page. Registration order is arbitrary to a viewer: Physarum 3D at position 1 and Physarum at 4; Turing Patterns at 43 and Reaction-Diffusion at 49; 12-fold at 36 and Aperiodic Tilings at 50. Two mitigations do exist and should survive: the end fade is live, and the active tab auto-scrolls into view on load.

**The strip stays. It stops being the only route.** Three pieces, in this order:

**Piece one, now: a filter input pinned at the left of the strip**, outside the scroller so it never scrolls away. It matches against `name`, `subtitle`, `credit`, `equation` and `blurb`, filters the strip in place, jumps to the first match on Enter, clears on Escape. One input and a substring match. That input has shipped. At 117 techniques it is no longer enough on its own — the Seen elsewhere filter sits next to it for the same reason.

**Piece two, now: translate vertical wheel deltas over `#tabs` into `scrollLeft`**, so an ordinary mouse works. Five lines.

**Piece three, later: a full technique browser**, opened from an All button at the right end of the strip and from a key. A grid of cards, one per technique, carrying the gallery thumbnail, the name, the subtitle and the credit year, with sort and filter controls above it. This is where sorting lives. Do not put sort controls on the strip; a horizontal scroller that reorders under you is worse than one that does not.

**The sort axes, and their provenance.** Five of the six are computed or cited. One is not, and that asymmetry is the design:

| Axis | Values | Where it comes from |
|---|---|---|
| Name | A to Z | the register |
| Family | 9 families (reaction-diffusion, phase separation, growth and aggregation, tilings and quasicrystals, lattice and statistical mechanics, flow and active matter, dynamical systems and orbits, waves and optics, geometry and number) | editorial taxonomy, defensible from the cited papers |
| Year | the paper's year | already in `subtitle` as text; promote it to a real `year` field in the register rather than parsing a string |
| Speed | steps per second, Still or Live | measured by `tools/check.js` |
| Print sharpness | edge acutance and acuity | measured by `tools/sharp.js` at 8 in and 300 ppi |
| **Familiarity** | 5 named buckets | **a curator's opinion, measured by nobody** |

**On the rarity axis, be explicit and be specific.** Call the field `familiarity`, not `rarity`, and run it from most seen to least seen, because \"rare\" implies scarcity in the world while \"familiarity\" plainly describes a viewer's experience, which is what the owner actually means. Present it in the UI as **\"How often you see it elsewhere\"**. Five named buckets, not a number:

1. **Ubiquitous** (Game of Life, fractal, flow fields)
2. **Common** (Turing patterns, reaction-diffusion, Penrose, strange attractors)
3. **Occasional** (Lenia, DLA, physarum, Chladni, KPZ)
4. **Rare** (Swift-Hohenberg, Ohta-Kawasaki, Liesegang, smectic, Toner-Tu)
5. **Almost unseen** (rotor-router, lozenge arctic ellipse, hyperbolic LERW, beta-ensembles)

Buckets rather than a 1-to-100 score, because a score implies a measurement and its granularity would be fabricated precision. Named buckets read as what they are: a judgement.

Four rules make it honest, and all four are required:

- **The control carries the caveat in its own label**, not in a tooltip or a footnote: `How often you see it elsewhere (a curator's call)`, with one sentence under it: `Nobody measured this. It is one person's estimate of how often you have seen the picture somewhere else, made in 2026. It is the only ordering in this studio that is not computed from the file.`
- **Every other axis carries its provenance in the same place, in the same type.** `year: from the cited paper. sharpness: measured by tools/sharp.js at 8 in and 300 ppi. speed: measured by tools/check.js.` The subjective axis is identified by contrast with labelled measurements, which is far stronger than a disclaimer sitting alone.
- **It is never the default sort.** Default is family. A subjective ordering that is on by default stops reading as an opinion and starts reading as the project's claim about the world.
- **The value lives in the module register** as `familiarity: 'rare'` next to `credit`, so it is visible in the source, and `tools/index.js` fails a module that omits it. A missing value must not silently default to the middle. It exports into `techniques.json` as the bucket string plus `familiaritySource: \"editorial\"`, and `TECHNIQUES.md` carries the same caveat sentence at the head of the column. Never emit a number.

## 4. What to leave alone, and what that tells you

**The thrown-out finding.** \"Switching tabs during a recording throws the clip away\" is false. `switchTo` calls `stopRecord` at `studio.html:2224`, `rec.start(250)` means chunks already exist, and `rec.onstop` saves them; on a genuinely Live plate the clip downloads. What the surveyor hit is that on a software rasterizer, attractors reads Still, and a Still plate produces no frames with or without a tab switch. Two lessons. First, any finding that depends on the witness verdict was measured on swiftshader and must be re-measured on real hardware before it is believed. Second, the real bug underneath is finding 41: `V` should not start a recording that is guaranteed to fail.

**The fonts.** Fixed at `e1eb72c`, with exactly the lint rule the finding asked for. Do not redo it. Do carry its consequence forward: every width in this survey is a fallback-font width.

**The roving tabindex.** Exactly 1 of the tabs has `tabIndex 0` (the survey counted 63; the rule is independent of the count). That is correct ARIA tablist behaviour and must survive the navigation work. The missing `role=\"tabpanel\"` and `aria-controls` are real but they are polish; do not let a correctness complaint about the ARIA drag the working part with it.

**The canvas already has an accessible name.** `aria-label=\"<technique> artwork\"` is present. Half of finding 17 was wrong.

**The export modal on a phone is already right.** The verifier drove the real flow at 390x844 and the modal shows the fully composed 2,400 px sheet, image inset in paper with title, equation, seed line, parameter block and swatches, above a labelled toggle, before any download. The finder's own proposed fix is what the code already does. Nothing structural. The only leftover is that the preview is 316 px wide, so let a tap open the sheet at full size; that helps on desktop too.

**The witness probe's cost.** The \"98.5 per cent of samples\" and \"31 s DOMContentLoaded\" numbers are profiler artifacts. The interval at `studio.html:3185` is already gated on `!document.hidden`, and the real marginal cost is mostly the readback waiting on GL work the simulation would do anyway. Do the interval backoff. Do **not** rewrite it around a scratch framebuffer on the strength of those numbers; measure on real GPU hardware first.

**The Penrose SVG's 506 off-artboard polygons** [47] cost file size and phantom objects in Illustrator. They do not affect printing: the outer `svg` clips to its viewBox by default and a 600x600 raster confirms it. Skip out-of-box polygons when convenient; do not schedule it.

**Chladni is not dotted.** A 1:1 crop of the same export shows continuous, solid nodal curves. Fix the style dispatch and the weight; ignore the dashes.

**The sticky 46vh stage on narrow screens is right.** The bug is that nothing else is pinned, not that the plate is.

**The `.tabs` hidden scrollbar and mask fade are deliberate**, and the fix for `.bar` is to match them, not to unhide scrollbars.

**The broader lesson.** Five of the surveyors' \"unreachable, no affordance\" claims were reachability claims the verifier disproved: shift+wheel scrolls the bar, six Tabs land on Export, `E` opens the modal, `bar.scrollLeft` works fine under touch, the strip's cut-off button is itself a standard hint. Meanwhile the two things that are genuinely unreachable, the seed box and the correct Penrose print, were confirmed by a different method than the one that found them. Severity should track what a person actually loses. A measurement that looks alarming is not the same as a loss.

---

## 5. Sequencing

**Now, batch 1, one sitting, all in the shell, no module touched.** The modal guard, the Space guard and the Escape reorder at `studio.html:3113-3135`; the `scheduleHash()` call sites; the `parseHash` try/catch and the unknown-id toast; the gallery overlay click; `V` on a Still plate; the `file://` service worker skip; `animation: none` under reduced motion; the focus-mode focus anchor; the About details default flip at `:2402`; the `[hidden]` rule; the two light-theme colour tokens; the three missing `title` attributes. Every one of these is small, and together they are the difference between a studio that loses your work and one that does not. Then `node tools/lint.js`.

**Now, batch 2: print integrity.** Penrose `exportSVG`, Chladni style dispatch and weight, the colophon art-size caption, the caption point size, `printSpec` reading `MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE`, the attractors point budget. Each lands with a harness assertion, and the important one is the plate-versus-print comparison in `/home/user/GENChase/tools/export.js`, run over every module with an `exportSVG`. `AGENTS.md` says this project has shipped bugs a thumbnail hid; this is that bug again, and it took a pixel comparison to catch it both times.

**Now, batch 3: layout, as one commit.** Seedbox `flex: 0 0 auto`, sticky-right print group, the `.bar` mask fade, the More sheet, the bottom dock below 900, `min-height: 0`, the short-viewport rule, the `dims` display rules, `46dvh`. These interact: fixing the seedbox alone adds 178 px to a bar that already overflows, so shipping it first makes the overflow worse. Re-measure everything with the inlined Geist faces before choosing breakpoint numbers.

**Now: navigation pieces one and two.** The filter input and the wheel translation. One input and five lines, and they are the whole near-term answer to a strip that no longer fits on the screen.

**Next: the WebGL LRU.** It is the only Tier 1 item that needs thought about lifecycle rather than a local edit, and it only bites a person who browses 17 tabs in a session. Real, but not this week.

**Can wait.** The technique browser with sort, filter and the familiarity axis; the keyboard poke across 24 modules; the touch-target sweep under `@media (pointer: coarse)` (138 elements under 44 px, all of them hittable today); `role=\"tabpanel\"` and `aria-controls`; the export progress note and cancel; the witness-hint pill; the export dialog header naming its technique and seed.

**A mistake to start.**

- **The technique browser before the filter input ships.** The input may make it unnecessary for a year, and the browser is where the subjective axis lives, which is the part worth getting slowly right.
- **Making familiarity the default sort, or giving it a number.** Both convert an opinion into a claim, in a project whose character is that it measures what it says.
- **Splitting `studio.html` or adding a build step to solve the layout.** `AGENTS.md` forbids it and the layout problem is about 40 lines of CSS.
- **Touching any module default while doing layout work.** Recipe v2 and the `legacy` declarations exist because a moved default silently reprints old recipes at a value they were never made at. That is a separate kind of change with its own test in `tools/recipe.js`, and it does not belong in a commit about flexbox.
- **Threading an export abort flag through every module.** Do the yield interval and the host-side progress note first.
- **Tuning any breakpoint to a number in this survey.** Fallback fonts.

**One standing item that outlasts all of it.** Not one of these 48 findings would have survived a harness that checked for it, and the harness is the thing this project already believes in. Add to `/home/user/GENChase/tools/ui.js`: `.seedbox` width greater than 150 at 390 and 1440; `#btn-export` right edge inside `innerWidth` at 390, 768 and 1440; no single-letter shortcut fires while a modal is open; the hash matches the plate after a roll and after a tab switch. Add the plate-versus-print comparison to `tools/export.js`. That is the durable output of this survey. The fixes are a week; the assertions are what keeps the week from being spent again."
